title: Merikoke and Massapequa Shared Lands
summary: The Merikoke/Merrick and Massapequa histories overlap across the south shore corridor, where source research describes kinship, refuge, shared territory, and alliance under colonial pressure.
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land with recognition of overlapping Merikoke/Merrick and Massapequa histories.
why_this_matters: Merikoke and Massapequa shared-land history challenges simple map boundaries. It shows Native communities responding to displacement through kinship, alliance, refuge, and shared use of south shore homelands.
introduction_content:
Local histories describe the Merikoke, also recorded with spellings such as Merrick and Mericock, in a south shore world closely connected with Massapequa communities. These accounts emphasize shared lands, kinship, tribute, refuge, and alliance rather than rigid modern boundaries.

Merrick ancestral land belongs to an interconnected Native geography stretching across waterways, meadows, necks, and neighboring communities.

source_list.title: Hempstead Town in Colonial Times, 1644-1783
